chats.answer:
For scanning a large automotive part as quickly as possible, I'd focus on industrial handheld 3D scanners with a large field of view and high-speed tracking.

The fastest scanner isn't necessarily the one advertising the most points per second. For large car parts—such as bumpers, doors, hoods, fenders, or chassis components—the important factors are:

Total scan time: How quickly you can capture the entire part.

Field of view: A larger scanning area means fewer passes.

Tracking: Whether you need to apply reference markers.

Accuracy: Whether you're scanning for reverse engineering, CAD, or simply capturing shape.

If speed is your top priority, here are the scanners I'd compare.

For scanning a large automotive part—such as a bumper, hood, fender, door, chassis, or engine block—the fastest option is usually a professional handheld 3D laser scanner with a large field of view, rather than a consumer-grade structured-light scanner.

The key distinction is between scanning speed (points per second) and total time to produce a complete, usable 3D model. A scanner with fewer points per second can finish faster if it captures a larger area in each pass and requires less repositioning.
